name: favourite-ring-wears-the-icon-palette
description: A favourite whose favicon carries several colours rings in all of them: the ring is a conic gradient with each colour at the angle it sits in the icon, the way the Microsoft and Google marks read. The fixture's icon is four quadrants, red top-left, green top-right, blue bottom-left, yellow bottom-right, on the same Dark space as the single-colour ring scenario. The tile is clicked so it selects, then the ring element's ::after is read: its background must be the palette gradient and its border must have stepped aside. The sibling favourite-ring-wears-the-icon-colour-in-glass proves a single red icon keeps the plain border.

actions.note: the only favourite tile, at a sibling scenario's coordinates. The click OPENS and CLAIMS the tab, which is what selects the tile.
the favourite has no live tab, so the click opens and claims one. The page spins for 3s, so this outlasts the load and the icon fetch
the Example tab row, so a push follows
the tile again, drawn from the icon the first visit stored

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.fav.sel'); if (!t) { return 'no selected tile'; } if (!t.classList.contains('palette')) { return 'no palette class'; } const grad = t.style.getPropertyValue('--ringgrad'); const stops = (grad.match(/rgb\([^)]*\) -?\d+deg/g) || []).length; const after = getComputedStyle(t.querySelector(':scope > .brdr'), '::after'); if (!after.backgroundImage.startsWith('conic-gradient')) { return 'border only: ' + after.backgroundImage; } if (after.borderTopColor !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)') { return 'border still painted: ' + after.borderTopColor; } return stops === 6 ? 'four colours around the ring' : 'stops ' + stops + ' ' + grad; })()
actions.note: The tile's first open fetches the site's root favicon.ico before the page's own PNG lands, so the icon in the database is the PNG only after that load. A second visit draws the tile from the PNG.

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: the selected tile's ring is the icon's four colours as a gradient, not one border colour
